quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
Stay one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in the side mirrors. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous. You need space to stop if the vehicle in front of you stops suddenly.

questions.question: Before stopping at a red light or stop sign, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator hard.
Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see what other cars are doing. Release the accelerator to slow down. Then move your foot to the brake and press steadily for a smooth stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Also watch the traffic in front of you and next to you.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Drive closely behind the car in front of you.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as possible.
Stay at a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Keep more space between you and the car in front of you. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. No one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to lose grip on wet road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the same speed to get better traction.
Brake hard to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually and do not brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not brake.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a regular car.
When following a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle stops or the rider falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous when driving in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch closely for workers and machines.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route to your destination.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Continue driving to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect a vehicle backing up and this will likely cause a crash.

questions.question: Hard, continuous braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Slow down before you need to brake hard to avoid this problem.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to fight the tiredness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop at a rest area or service station to nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work zones:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light signals.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals control traffic flow and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey these signals unless a police officer is directing traffic instead.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Just the driver
Only children
All people in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: All people in the vehicle
questions.explanation: Wyoming law requires all vehicle occupants to wear a safety belt. The driver is responsible for making sure everyone obeys this law. Children must use proper child-restraint systems.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this exact speed.
The maximum speed limit under good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum legal speed on this road. You can drive slower if road conditions require it, but you cannot drive faster than this speed limit.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears before turning. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep driving at your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads make your tires grip less than dry roads do. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow closer to the car ahead.
Drive through carefully and do not stare at the workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully and do not stare at the workers.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at construction work or workers. This causes traffic to slow down. Keep your eyes on the road ahead.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas you cannot see when you are tired.
Areas around your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to go. Check the areas near the rear corners of your vehicle. Your mirrors cannot show these areas, so they are called blind spots.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you and creates danger. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car moves in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the car ahead without hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used to:

options.text: Mark areas where you cannot pass.
Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see flashing red lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Stop completely.
Try to go around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing signs warn you that a train may be coming. You must obey all railroad warning signs and lights. Never try to drive around barriers.

questions.question: What do defensive drivers do?

options.text: Trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
Think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
Expect no breaks and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting errors from other drivers and being prepared to react to their mistakes.

questions.question: As you drive faster, it is important to:

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, your stopping distance increases. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to safely react to dangers.

questions.question: You are in a minor car crash at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your car in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your car out of the traffic lane if you can.
Never move your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries or deaths, you should move your car out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any car, bicycle, or person in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any car, bicycle, or person in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any cars, bicycles, or people still in the intersection.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, do not brake. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of large trucks or buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to alert tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Remove your foot from the accelerator and do not brake. Let the car slow on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit, but you cannot drive faster. You must reduce speed on curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and roads with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, you should yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road are:

options.text: Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
Not required to follow rules of the road.
Always required to yield to motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers should respect the rights of cyclists.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular, white and red.
Round or octagonal, black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular, orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular, orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns and curves.
Traffic is increasing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that the road will be slippery when wet and they should slow down.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before making a left turn. Keep your front wheels pointing straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street so you can:

options.text: See hazards early.
Have enough room to stop your vehicle.
Keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: See hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles entering at on-ramps and expect sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: If you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other cars and people crossing.

questions.question: On a road with a broken white centerline, you may:

options.text: Stay in your lane only.
Cross the line to change lanes.
Change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the line to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in that direction if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed with a green arrow if you are in the right lane, even if other signals show red. Always let pedestrians and other vehicles pass first.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Bicycles on roadways are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bike riders and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Follow the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's signals, even if they contradict traffic lights, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: Motorcycles on the road:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as other motor vehicles.
Do not need to follow traffic rules.
Must always give way to larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as cars and trucks. Other drivers should respect motorcycle riders' rights.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is about to end. Be ready to let oncoming traffic go.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road ahead will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a divided highway begins ahead. Stay to the right of the center divider.
